observations: Industrial sewing machine on a white metal table.
The brand 'TAKI' is visible on the side of the machine in photo 2.
The machine has a large motor mounted underneath the table.
A vertical thread stand with multiple spools is attached to the table.
The table surface has a ruler marked in centimeters.
The machine is plugged into a wall socket.
The floor around the machine is cluttered with fabric scraps and a measuring tape.

claims.evidence: The brand 'TAKI' is visible in photo 2, which is different from EMel.
No model number is legible on the machine in any photo.
No Japanese flag or 'Made in Japan' stamp is visible on the machine.

claims.claim: the motor runs smooth. All accessories and the original manual, never serviced because nothing ever went wrong.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The machine may not stitch or may have a broken needle bar.
risks.proof: A video of the machine stitching a piece of fabric.

risks.risk: The motor may be weak or overheating.
risks.proof: A video of the motor running for several minutes.

risks.risk: The table may be unstable or the stand may be rusted.
risks.proof: A photo of the table surface and the underside of the stand.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Video of the machine stitching fabric to prove it works.
Video of the motor running to check for noise or overheating.
Photo of the underside of the table to check for rust or damage.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
